title: Proposed 24-hour patient cancellation rule

known_current_implementation_evidence.online_change_gate: min_change_notice_minutes defaults to 120; patient cancellation is rejected when the appointment starts less than this many minutes after the current instant.
known_current_implementation_evidence.late_cancellation_flag: tenants.late_cancel_hours defaults to 24; this sets a late_cancel classification flag and does not itself reject cancellation.
known_current_implementation_evidence.staff_and_system: Scheduling.cancel bypasses the online change-window guard for staff and system actors.
known_current_implementation_evidence.interpretation: The current 120-minute gate and 24-hour late-cancel flag are separate behaviours. The proposed 24-hour denial rule is not currently proven or implemented.

known_postman_request_evidence.evidence_limit: Collection request shape only; not proof of status codes or response schema.

open_questions: Does the proposed change alter the patient cancellation gate from 120 minutes to 24 hours?
Is the threshold based on elapsed duration or local wall-clock time across daylight-saving transitions?
